account: It is just after noon on day 0, and I am home for my scheduled lunch. So far I have no solid evidence of anything secret or unusual, despite my feeling that something may be happening without me. During the morning market walk, several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. Later, two townsfolk independently told me the baker had carried a sack of bread at the inn. I also saw the baker restock the market bread chest and bought two fresh loaves. These movements could simply be normal baking, deliveries, and sales; I do not know of any other purpose. My question about unusual gatherings or concerns has yielded no specific report. A lantern appeared near the town hall this morning, but I do not know who placed it or why. The secretary had no correspondence or town news to report. The appointment book lists tea at three with an unnamed neighbour at an unspecified east-bank dockside cottage. That lack of detail is worth resolving, but is not evidence of a secret meeting. The secretary said she would inquire. I intend to attend town accounts at the office at one, check the treasury personally, and ask whether she has identified my tea host and address. For now, the baker's deliveries, the new lantern, and the vague tea appointment are observations to clarify, not grounds for accusing anyone.
